metadata.note: The Tampa and Gulf Coast, the railroad that put Pinellas County's second line on the map. Its first road (1910) ran from the Tampa Northern at Lutz west to Tarpon Springs; in 1914 it built from Gulf Coast Junction (Sulphur Springs) across the head of Old Tampa Bay through Oldsmar and Safety Harbor to Clearwater and south via Belleair, Largo and Bay Pines to St. Petersburg, re-routed the Tarpon Springs line onto a new connector from Rocky Creek, and added branches to Port Richey (bought 1912) and Indian Rocks Beach (1915). The Seaboard Air Line bought the stock about 1915 and leased the road in 1927. The main line carried SAL through trains to St. Petersburg until the 1967 merger; the Seaboard Coast Line and then Amtrak used it as far as Clearwater (then the ex-ACL line to St. Petersburg) until Amtrak left Pinellas County on 1 Feb 1984. The ex-T&GC grade Belleair - St. Petersburg is now the Pinellas Trail, and the Rocky Creek - Lake Fern connector the Upper Tampa Bay Trail. Not in this file: the ACL (ex-Orange Belt) Trilby - Tarpon Springs - Clearwater - St. Petersburg line, a different railroad that also called itself the Orange Belt.

properties.line: Tampa and Gulf Coast: Tampa – St. Petersburg
properties.speed_source: estimated: the May 1917 schedule (Evening Leader, 6 Dec 1917) gives Lv Tampa 7:50, Ar St Petersburg 10:20 - about 54 mi in 2.5 h - but the OCR is partly mangled; treat as an estimate
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (CSX Clearwater Subdivision; Pinellas Trail ways tagged old_railway_operator=SAL), checked against OpenHistoricalMap
properties.geometry_quality: Traced with opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap. Tampa Union Station - Gulf Coast Junction (Sulphur Springs) is the ex-Tampa Northern trackage (ICC: 5.37 mi) on CSX track (ACL-tagged Tampa Terminal Subdivision, then untagged CSX Clearwater/Brooksville Subdivision ways) via Ybor; Gulf Coast Jn - Oldsmar - Safety Harbor - Clearwater - Belleair is the live CSX Clearwater Subdivision (untagged ways, checked against OpenHistoricalMap's 'Tampa & Gulf Coast Railroad' ways -200853862 / -200836510 / -200717149, which it overlays); Belleair - Largo - Seminole - Bay Pines - Pasadena - Gulfport - 34th St S is the Pinellas Trail on ways tagged old_railway_operator=SAL (FDOT bought this right of way in 1983). Sampled against OHM: every SAL-tagged Pinellas Trail way south of 27.95 N lies 0.0 km from OHM's T&GC way and 1-7 km from OHM's 'ACL St. Petersburg Branch' - so this is the T&GC grade, not the ex-ACL (Orange Belt) grade, which the Pinellas Trail follows only north of the Belleair crossing. Straight-line legs: one, 0.5 mi, from the end of the mapped trail at 27.769 N -82.654 along 2nd Avenue South to the old SAL depot at 9th Street (the grade is mapped there only as fragments tagged on 2nd Avenue South). Traced length 54.1 mi Tampa Union Station - St. Petersburg, against 53.9 mi by the 1952 Official Guide's SAL mileposts (850.3-904.2) and 52.86 mi by the ICC valuation (47.49 owned + 5.37 trackage); 51.1 mi by the SY mileposts Wikipedia prints. Station check against the 1952 Guide (miles from Tampa, traced/Guide): Oldsmar 20.5/20.2, Safety Harbor 25.2/25.1, Clearwater 32.7/32.7, Largo 36.5/36.0, Bay Pines 43.6/42.4. The St. Petersburg end is drawn to the original 2nd Ave S & 9th St depot; the 1959 SAL station at 34th St S lies on the drawn line. Later-alignment note: Tampa approaches are drawn on today's CSX track layout through Ybor, which may differ in detail from the 1914 Tampa Northern / Union Station approach.

segments.note: Gulf Coast Junction (Sulphur Springs) - Clearwater opened 1 April 1914 and Clearwater - St. Petersburg 22 September 1914 (ICC valuation). Trains reached Tampa Union Station over 5.37 mi of Tampa Northern trackage, under a 14 May 1914 Union Station lease. Passenger service is directly confirmed by T&GC timetables printed in the Tarpon Springs Evening Leader on 7 Dec 1916 and 6 Dec 1917 (effective 20 May 1917: two Tampa - St. Petersburg trains via Safety Harbor, Clearwater, Belleair, Largo and Indian Beach). The ICC "opened" dates are not themselves passenger evidence; 1914-1915 are assumed from them. The road advertised itself as the "Orange Belt Route" - not the ACL Orange Belt line, a different road. The Seaboard Air Line owned all the stock from about 1915, but the T&GC "was operated by its own organization" until 28 Dec 1917 (ICC). Headway (two trains a day) is an estimate from the 1917 schedule.
sources: Segment-level: opening dates from the ICC valuation report (vol. 35, valuation date 1917); passenger trains from the Evening Leader timetables of Dec 1916 and Dec 1917. Confirmed passenger years 1916-1917 only; 1914-1915 inferred from the opening dates.

segments.note: USRA federal control from 28 Dec 1917 to 29 Feb 1920 (ICC confirms from 1 Jan 1918), then the T&GC again in its own right (a 1923 Transportation Act guaranty settlement with the T&GC, ICC). Ends at 1926, the last year before the Seaboard Air Line lease (ICC Finance Docket 5950, decided 8 Jan 1927). NO DATED TIMETABLE FOUND FOR 1918-1926: passenger continuity in these years is interpolated between the 1917 schedule and the SAL era, not individually dated. A Sulphur Springs depot was built in 1924 (Wikipedia) - weak corroboration only. Headway is an estimate.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: no 1918-1926 timetable has been checked; the span is interpolated between the 1917 T&GC schedule and the 1927 SAL lease. The lease date comes from an ICC Monthly Catalog search snippet (page returned 503, wording not verified).

segments.note: Seaboard Air Line era, from the 1927 lease of the T&GC (ICC Finance Docket 5950, decided 8 Jan 1927; "fully integrated with the SAL system in 1927"; Janet Lewis, West Pasco's Heritage: "leased to the Seaboard Air Line Railway in 1927") to the SAL/ACL merger of 1 July 1967, after which the SAL no longer ran the trains. Through trains from the North and Midwest: Orange Blossom Special (west-coast section, winter), Silver Meteor, Florida Sunbeam, Southern States Special, New York-Florida Limited, Palmland. The February 1952 Official Guide (SAL Table 7, "Wildwood, Tampa and St. Petersburg", dated 13 Dec 1951) shows rail times Tampa - Sulphur Springs - Oldsmar - Safety Harbor - Clearwater - Belleair - Largo - Bay Pines - St. Petersburg, with trains 107/157/121/1/27; Table 12 runs St. Petersburg - Miami via the Cross-Florida line. New SAL St. Petersburg station at 34th St S built 1959. Confirmed passenger years: 1940, 1942, 1951, 1956, 1959. The exact 1927 date SAL crews took over is not known. Headway is an estimate from the 1952 table.
sources: Segment-level: 1952 Official Guide SAL Tables 7 and 12 (passenger trains Tampa - St. Petersburg via Clearwater); lease year from ICC Finance Docket 5950 via the ICC Monthly Catalog (snippet only); 1940/1942/1956/1959 service from the Wikipedia articles and chicagorailfan timetable extracts; end = 1 Jul 1967 merger.

properties.line: Seaboard Coast Line: Tampa – St. Petersburg (via Clearwater)
properties.speed_source: estimated; not computed from a timetable
properties.geometry_quality: Traced with opstrace.py over OpenStreetMap, all on live CSX Clearwater Subdivision track (untagged ways, 45.9 mi) plus 0.6 mi of ACL-tagged Tampa Terminal Subdivision at Tampa. Tampa Union Station - Gulf Coast Jn is ex-Tampa Northern; Gulf Coast Jn - Clearwater - Belleair is the ex-T&GC/SAL line (shared geometry with the T&GC and SAL features in this file); from the Belleair crossing the trace leaves the ex-SAL grade and follows the ex-ACL (Orange Belt) line, still CSX track, south-east through Largo and Pinellas Park to the 1963 ACL station at 3601 31st St N. No straight-line legs. Traced length 46.5 mi; Tampa - Clearwater 32.7 mi against SAL milepost 850.3-883.0 (32.7). The connection point between the two Pinellas lines is drawn at the Belleair crossing, which is where today's CSX track joins them (WP-TGC); Wikipedia's Clearwater Subdivision article instead places a 1967 crossover at North Clearwater, MP SY 873.0 - CONFLICT recorded, affects about 2 mi of geometry. Later-alignment note: this is the modern CSX layout; any post-1984 track changes at the junction are not distinguished.

segments.note: After the SAL/ACL merger of 1 July 1967 the Seaboard Coast Line consolidated St. Petersburg passenger service at the ex-ACL station on 31st St N (1963) and ran the St. Petersburg sections of the Silver Star and Champion over the ex-T&GC/SAL line Tampa - Clearwater, then the ex-ACL Orange Belt line to St. Petersburg (Wikipedia, citing the SCL 1970 employee timetable and Luisi 2010). Only Gulf Coast Junction - Clearwater/Belleair is ex-T&GC; Tampa - Gulf Coast Jn is ex-Tampa Northern and Belleair - St. Petersburg is ex-ACL. Ends 1 May 1971 when Amtrak took over. Whether any SCL train still used the ex-SAL line south of Belleair after the merger is not established, so that piece is not drawn for SCL. Headway is an estimate (two sections daily).
sources: Segment-level: Wikipedia articles on the Tampa and Gulf Coast, the Clearwater Subdivision and the Amtrak St. Petersburg station (citing the SCL 1970 employee timetable and Luisi 2010) - secondary sources only; the 1970 timetable itself was not seen.

properties.line: Tampa and Gulf Coast: Tarpon Springs Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated: the May 1917 schedule gives Lv Tampa 3:30 pm, Ar Tarpon Springs 7:00 pm (about 35 mi via Rocky Creek) - an estimate, possibly a mixed train
properties.geometry_source: OpenStreetMap (Upper Tampa Bay Trail and abandoned ways tagged old_railway_operator=SAL) and OpenHistoricalMap
properties.geometry_quality: Traced with opstrace.py. Rocky Creek (Tarpon Junction) - Citrus Park - north of Citrus Park: the Upper Tampa Bay Trail, OSM ways tagged old_railway_operator=SAL, and OHM way -198646208 (unnamed) on the same grade; Lake Fern - Gulf Pine: OHM way -201534234 'Tampa & Gulf Coast Railway'; Gulf Pine - west of Gulf Pine: OHM way -198646209 (unnamed); east of East Lake - Lake Villa: OSM way 655027507 tagged old_railway_operator=SAL (4.4 mi) and ways 1151666511-13; Tarpon Springs terminal: East Lemon Street, tagged old_railway_operator=SAL. Straight-line legs (3, total 4.6 mi): end of mapped grade at 28.136 N - Lake Fern, 1.6 mi; west of Gulf Pine (-82.625) - east end of SAL way 655027507 (-82.641), 1.0 mi; west end of the SAL ways at -82.721 - East Lemon Street, Tarpon Springs, 2.0 mi (the grade through east Tarpon Springs is not mapped). Traced length 21.9 mi against 21.5 mi documented (Rocky Creek SYA 856.3 - Tarpon Springs 877.8; Fowler 0.0-21.5). Station check (miles from Rocky Creek, traced/documented SYA): Lake Fern 8.6/8.0, Gulf Pine 11.1/10.3, Lake Villa 18.9/18.1. Drawn from 1914 only: the Rocky Creek - Lake Fern leg opened 18 Mar 1914, and before that trains reached Lake Fern from Lutz (separate feature).

segments.note: Tarpon Junction (Rocky Creek) - Lake Fern opened 18 March 1914 (ICC), joining the 1910 Lake Fern - Gulf Pine - Lake Villa - Tarpon Springs line, whose Lutz connection was then abandoned. Passenger trains confirmed by the Dec 1916 T&GC advertisement (Tampa - Tarpon Springs) and the schedule effective 20 May 1917: "3:30 P.M. Lv Tampa ... 7:00 P.M. Ar Tarpon Springs", continuing to Sans Souci and Port Richey. 1914-1915 are inferred from the opening date. Terminal "less than a block" from the ACL depot in Tarpon Springs. Headway (one train each way) is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation (18 Mar 1914 opening of Tarpon Jn - Lake Fern) and the Evening Leader timetables of Dec 1916 and Dec 1917. Confirmed passenger years 1916-1917 only.

segments.note: USRA 1918 - Feb 1920, then T&GC to the 1927 SAL lease. NO DATED TIMETABLE FOUND for 1918-1926: continuity interpolated. The branch is not drawn under the SAL at all: the 1952 Official Guide marks Gulf Pine, Keystone and Cosme "for freight only" and SAL-era passenger service has not been found; when passengers ended (anywhere from 1918 to before 1951) is unknown. Headway is an estimate.
sources: NOT SOURCED AT SEGMENT LEVEL: no 1918-1926 timetable checked; span interpolated between the 1917 schedule and the 1927 lease.

properties.line: Tampa and Gulf Coast: Lutz – Tarpon Springs (original line)
properties.geometry_source: Lutz Lake Fern Road centreline (OSM) for the lifted Lutz - Lake Fern leg; OpenHistoricalMap and OSM beyond
properties.geometry_quality: Pre-1914 alignment, drawn as its own feature and NOT on the post-1914 Rocky Creek route. Lutz (junction with the Tampa Northern, here the CSX Brooksville Subdivision node at 28.151 N) - Lake Fern: the grade is not mapped in OSM or OHM; drawn along the centreline of Lutz Lake Fern Road (6.7 mi), the road whose name and course (due west from Lutz to Lake Fern at about 28.155 N, ending where OHM's 1909 'Tampa & Gulf Coast Railway' way begins) follow the old line - an inference, not a confirmed road-on-grade; treat this leg as approximate to within a few hundred metres. Lake Fern - Gulf Pine: OHM way -201534234 'Tampa & Gulf Coast Railway' (start_date 1909); Gulf Pine onward to Tarpon Springs shares geometry with the Tarpon Springs Branch feature, including its two straight legs (west of Gulf Pine - east end of SAL way 655027507, 1.0 mi; -82.721 - East Lemon Street, Tarpon Springs, 2.0 mi). Traced length 20.3 mi against 21-22 mi documented (ICC: Lutz - Gulf Pine 10, Gulf Pine - Tarpon Springs 11); traced Lutz - Gulf Pine 9.5 mi.

segments.note: The original T&GC line, built by the Tampa and Gulf Coast Railway Company (inc. 1909; sold to the Tampa and Gulf Coast Railroad Company 19 May 1913 - same name and corridor, a reorganisation, one colour): Lutz (junction with the Tampa Northern, over which trains ran to Tampa) - Lake Fern - Gulf Pine (ex-Gulf Pine Company logging road, bought 17 Sep 1909) - Keystone - Lake Villa - Tarpon Springs (built Sept 1909 - Sept 1910). "Placed in operation in September, 1910" (ICC); "By September 1910, trains offered regular passenger and freight service over 21 miles of track" (Patch); in 1913-14 "four passenger stops daily, one round trip Tarpon Springs to Tampa" (Glen Dill, Suncoast News 1988). No primary 1910-1913 timetable has been found. Lutz - Lake Fern was abandoned after the Rocky Creek connector opened 18 Mar 1914; 1914 itself is left to the Tarpon Springs Branch feature. Headway (one round trip) from Dill, otherwise an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation (Sept 1910 opening) with secondary passenger statements from Patch (community history column) and Glen Dill (Suncoast News, Aug 1988, via the West Pasco Historical Society) - no contemporaneous timetable seen.

properties.line: Tampa and Gulf Coast: Port Richey Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated; not computed from a timetable
properties.geometry_quality: Traced with opstrace.py, no straight-line legs. Lake Villa Junction - Elfers: OSM abandoned-railway ways 1271032293 / 1271030353 and 1271030352 (named 'Seaboard Air Line', no operator tag); Elfers - New Port Richey - Port Richey: OHM ways 'Tampa & Gulf Coast Railroad - New Port Richey Branch' (-200818649 / -200818650 / -200818639). The westward 'Seaboard Air Line' way 1271030354 / Elfers Spur Trail towards the Anclote coast is a different (later SAL) spur and is NOT drawn. Traced length 6.9 mi against 7.01 mi (ICC) / 7.0 mi (SYB Lake Villa 874.7 - Port Richey 881.7). The northern terminal is drawn at the end of OHM's branch way, 28.250 N, consistent with the 2.3 mi Elfers - Port Richey milepost spacing; Elfers traced 4.5 mi from Lake Villa against 4.7 by SYB mileposts.

segments.note: Lake Villa Junction - Sans Souci - Elfers - New Port Richey - Port Richey, bought from J. M. Weeks & Company in December 1912 (ICC). Start is the first CONFIRMED passenger year: the Dec 1916 T&GC advertisement names Port Richey, and the 1917 schedule runs the 3:30 pm Tampa train on via Tarpon Springs and Sans Souci to Port Richey. Earlier service is claimed but conflicting - "semi-weekly service" from summer 1913 (Patch), trains "twice weekly" (Dill), "has operated here since 1916" (Evening Independent, 3 May 1943) - so 1913-1915 is withheld. 1918-1926 is interpolated (no dated timetable) to the 1927 SAL lease. Not drawn under the SAL: the New Port Richey depot closed 25 Apr 1943 with the Elfers - NPR rails lifted, and the Jan 1952 Guide prints "Elfers Branch ... Freight Service only"; no SAL-era passenger evidence was found and when passengers ended is unknown. Headway is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: the Evening Leader timetables of Dec 1916 and Dec 1917 name Port Richey; acquisition date from the ICC valuation. 1918-1926 not individually sourced.

properties.line: Tampa and Gulf Coast: Indian Beach Branch
properties.speed_source: estimated; not computed from a timetable
properties.geometry_source: straight-line approximation (no surviving grade in OSM or OHM)
properties.geometry_quality: NOT TRACED - no grade survives in OSM or OpenHistoricalMap. Two straight-line legs: Indian Beach Junction (on the main line, placed 3.6 mi south of the Belleair crossing from the SY mileposts 876.1 / 879.7) - Anona hamlet, 1.9 mi; Anona - Indian Rocks Beach (town centroid, across the Narrows), 0.9 mi. Drawn length 2.8 mi against 3.10 mi (ICC) / 2.6 mi (Fowler 887.9-890.5) / 2.6 mi (SYC 879.7-882.3). The real route and the drawbridge site are unknown.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] [OPEN] Indian Beach Junction (Largo) - Anona - Indian Beach (Indian Rocks Beach), across Clearwater Bay (the Narrows) on a drawbridge; built Dec 1914 - June 1915 (ICC), right of way, grading and bridge owned by the Indian Beach Company. 1917 is the ONLY confirmed passenger year: the schedule effective 20 May 1917 shows "Ar Indian Beach" in the Tampa - St. Petersburg table. Service certainly ran wider in both directions - from about 1915, and "declined in the 1920s" before the bridge was removed by 1928 - but no other year is confirmed, so none is drawn. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when passenger service actually stopped. Do not widen this anchor without evidence, and do not delete it to tidy the map. The Indian Beach Jn - Anona stub that lasted to the early 1940s was freight and is not drawn. Headway is an estimate (seasonal beach traffic).
sources: Segment-level: the Evening Leader of 6 Dec 1917 (schedule effective 20 May 1917) lists Indian Beach; construction dates from the ICC valuation. Single anchored year.
